newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, March 18 - No labour probls. Haifa - Eight vessels operating of which 3 discharging at berth (2 general cargo, 1 bulker), 4 containers, 1 tanker. 5 Vessels waiting at anchor of which 2 to discharge (1 general cargo, 1 bulker), 1 container vessel, 2 tankers. 2 Vessels under repair/dry-docked, 4 awaiting orders, 4 due with 1-2 days delay expected. Ashdod - 24 Vessels operating of which 16 discharging at berth (8 general cargo, 8 bulkers). 1 Bulker loading at berth, 3 containers, 2 car carriers, 1 tanker, 1 passenger vessel. 19 Vessels waiting at anchor of which 14 to discharge (13 general cargo, 1 bulker). 2 Bulkers to load, 3 container vessels, 1 vessel awaiting orders, 2-4 days berthing delay expected at present. Eilat - Two vessels operating of which 1 bulker loading at berth, 1 passenger vessel, 1 tanker waiting at anchorage.

MOZAMBIQUE, March 17 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions - 9.5 Metres at general cargo berth and 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally, 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation - 7.5 metres. Two tugs available.

General access channel - Two waverider buoys have been deployed in the approach channel as follows - WMON1 - 19 deg.6.0460 s 36 deg. 01.6698 e and WMON2 - 19 deg. 62.6370 s 34 deg. 62.6497 e. Each buoy has an approximate diameter of 1 metre, with flashing orange light with a flash frequency of five one-second flashes every 36 seconds. Maputo - Twenty-four hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so. Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.metres (ukc) plus the rise of tide. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, March 17 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, March 17 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Fully committed. Bulk import berths - Fully committed. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Fully committed. Bulk coal berths - At present 4 vessels berthed and 6 vessels at the anchorage and 3 arriving 17/3. A further 15 vessels are due up to and including 24/3, with delays of 3-4 days being experienced, but this was expected to drop to 2-3 days. Durban - Container terminal - Some vessels experiencing delays of up to 60 hours, whilst others berthing on arrival. Point/New pier/Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - One vessel. Bunker supplies - Product available but this could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully booked until the end of March and 70 percent full for April.

East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Very busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Fully booked up to 24/3, thereafter open. Copper - Moving in small parcels of 2,500 metric tonnes per month in containers to the Far East. Gas oil pipelines - Under utilised. Tankers - Expected to be busy until the end of March. Scrap steel - 1,500 Tonnes on hand. Port Elizabeth - Working normally, with 3 vessel in port. No delays expected on general, ore, tanker or fruit berths. Container berth - An additional gantry crane is expected to arrive in April from Durban. Two vessels due 18/3, one of which can expect about 5 hours delay. A further 3 vessels are due 20/3, one of which will experience about 4 hours delay.

Cape Town - Container terminal - Vessels working and berthing on arrival, no delays expected for the coming week. Breakbulk berths - Working normally, with vessels berthing/operating on arrival. Fruit berths - Expected to be fully occupied for the coming week. Bunker berths - No delays expected for the coming week. Dry-docks and repair quays - Fully occupied. Booking is essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, March 15 - Sfax - Seven vessels in port operating of which 2 discharging (1 bulk maize, 1 bulk sulphur). 4 Loading (1 bulk rock phosphate, 1 bulk tsp, 1 other), 1 other vessel. Sousse - Four vessels in port, all discharging, of which 1 bagged sugar, 1 cotton, 1 general cargo, 1 big bags. No waiting time, no vessels awaiting orders. March 18 - Bizerte - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Six vessels in port, all discharging, of which 1 sugar, 1 fuel oil, 1 pumice stone, 1 steel, 1 iron ore, 1 cement.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, March 9-15 - Dubai - 185 Vessels of which 83 containers, 14 general cargo, 2 general cargo/containers, 2 bulk carriers, 5 car carriers, 14 tankers, 4 naval vessels, 6 taking bunkers/stores/under repair etc., 6 dhows, 11 barges, 9 tugs, 23 supply boats, 3 passenger vessels, 1 fishing trawler, 2 diving support vessels. 15 Vessels loading/discharging at berth (2 containers, 10 general cargo, 3 tankers). 6 Under repair/laid-up (2 general cargo, 4 tankers). 39 Vessels due (29 containers, 6 general cargo, 3 tankers).

YEMEN, March 17 - Hodeidah - Berths occupied except for no. 6. Seven vessels berthed of which 1 bulk wheat, 1 sugar, 3 general, 1 steel, 1 wheatflour. 2 Anchored (1 flour, 1 bulk wheat). Delays, general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargoes to 3 days, bulk up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - One wheatflour vessel berthed, none anchored, no delays.
